questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose to apply for an exchange semester in Bern, Switzerland, because I had never visited the country before and had heard many positive things about it. I have a strong interest in macroeconomics and in the direction the world is developing, especially at the time when I applied. Europe seemed to be facing increasing pressure to strengthen its position relative to the United States in many ways, and I therefore thought it would be exciting to experience Switzerland firsthand. Although Switzerland is not part of the European Union, it has a strong economy and many unique and interesting institutions, making it a particularly fascinating place to study economics.
I was also motivated by the location of Bern. I love mountains and skiing, so Bern is perfect for that. 
I wanted to improve my German. As it turned out, that only happened to a limited extent, since people in Bern primarily speak Swiss German. I had read positive things about the university in Bern, and I mistakenly believed that studying in Zurich required proficiency in French, which is why I did not apply there. That turned out not to be true, but by coincidence I ended up exactly where I was supposed to be.

Bern’s location is perfect for travelling around Switzerland, especially if you enjoy the mountains. The train connections from Bern to the rest of the country are excellent, making it easy to explore both cities and alpine regions.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of administrative work to take care of before leaving. However, Bern University responded very quickly and was helpful throughout the process.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Quite a lot. The University of Bern had organized a full orientation week for exchange students, where we had the opportunity to meet other international students and receive plenty of useful information, tips, and practical advice for our stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite tough at first, but I got lucky. I used a Facebook group for Danes in Switzerland to find a shared flat with a lovely Swiss girl, very central.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Watch out for scammers – it is expensive to live there, so people have an incentive to scam exchange students. I recommend getting a bike to get around the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very conscious that I wanted to live locally in order to get to know Swiss friends and experience the culture firsthand. I live in a student dorm in Copenhagen, so I was also motivated to try living with fewer people, since I expected that the social life at the university would already take up a lot of time and energy. However, I did end up making friends who lived in student dorms, and they also had a great experience, just a different one.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to get two elective courses approved, which took a long time and required me to take several courses in Bern in order to match the courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is very easy, and you can typically change your courses during the first week or so.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Bern University is is very helpful and usually responds within a day when you contact them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful in the end, but I was also very aware of when registration opened, as some of the important courses had limited seats.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the courses at the university before you apply. Try to plan your week so you have days without classes to explore and have fun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teaching style is a bit old-fashioned compared to the University of Copenhagen, but the academic level is comparable. I took master’s-level courses, so the classes were very small, which was great, as it allowed me to build relationships with both the lecturers and the other students despite the short time. The exam period is tough – they squeeze all the exams into one week, with no time to catch up beforehand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am doing my bachelor’s in Copenhagen, so I can’t say much about the master’s courses there. I think the level is comparable, maybe slightly lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar, but with less material from the lectures to prepare with, which I missed during the exam period.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Macroeconomics II, Doing Economics with the Computer, Modern Time Series Econometrics, Econometrics II, 
Environmental Econometrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They were great. Macro III was very old-school, with no PowerPoint slides and a tricky exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I spent some money on different ski courses offered by the university, and skipass to Verbie, which I would highly recommend. Great value for money and some of the best skiing of my life.

In Switzerland, they are very strict and precise with deadlines, so I ended up paying some fines due to late registration for certain things, and I also received a train ticket on the first day. They really follow the rules.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food from the supermarket is not as bad as people say, but eating out is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I used the facilities at Unisport a lot. They offer all kinds of sports, most of them for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many social and academic clubs, and as mentioned before, plenty of sports opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Skiing! And hiking as much as possible in the weekends with your new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore! There are so many cool places to see, and easy acces from Bern. Everything in Switzerland is beautiful, and it’s a great way to bond with new friends because you spend the whole day together with very little use of phones.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Easy. Similar to danish people, maybe a bit more reserved, but you’ll find your way. Remember you are there for a short time, so take chances and say hello. You might even get invited to someone’s ski cabin or go dancing at Bierhübeli ;)
One tip - BE ON TIME. It really matters in Schweizerland.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They joke less, but have humor for sure.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The sense of order and the reliability of people, trains, and commitments really stood out to me. I also really appreciated how much people value and use the surrounding nature. The locals often go hiking in the mountains on weekends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don’t stress too much about the courses. Enjoy your time and make as many connections as you can. Say yes to more than you feel like at first. Get a train pass and don’t be afraid to ask other exchange students if they want to join you. Many of my best friends from exchange came about quite randomly, simply from being open to meeting new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to sign up for the exams, not just the courses, and get a bike.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends, academic challenges and success, skiing, and getting to know Swiss culture. I feel very privileged to have been able to find a sense of home in another country, and that is thanks to all the locals and exchange students I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academics and managing the balance between studying a lot and exploring as much as possible.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
